evidence: The statement says "Any valid allocation is accepted"; the surviving solution uses "order vertices by degree descending" and bitmask backtracking, which can stop after finding one coloring.
removal_suggestion: Require the lexicographically smallest valid sequence z_1, z_2, ..., z_n instead of accepting an arbitrary valid allocation.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses bitmask-based exact 3-coloring with descending-degree vertex ordering and can return the first solution found.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The implementation reaches a runtime error in its bitmask/DSATUR-style solver rather than producing an answer.
It uses essentially unpruned recursive backtracking in input/node order, causing exponential search and a time-limit failure on hard 3-coloring instances.

recommended_edit: Replace "Any valid allocation is accepted" with a requirement to output the lexicographically smallest valid allocation.
